title: Direct whole-cell patch-clamp recordings from small boutons in rodent primary neocortical neuron cultures
protocol: Cut glass capillary into ∼5 cm lengths using a triangular file.
Clean glass dust from the cut ends using compressed air spray or wipe with finger.
Pull quartz glass pipettes from capillaries.
Inspect pipettes individually at low magnification for taper shape.
Inspect pipettes individually at intermediate magnification for taper shape.
Inspect pipettes individually at high magnification for pipette intactness and tip opening diameter.
Fill pipette tips with minimal internal recording solution using Microloader™ pipette tips.
Shorten pipettes to minimal length such that the electrode fits under the condenser.
Clean cut ends of glass dust and mount on pipette holder.
Insert coverslip into bath chamber.
Stabilize position with a metal grid if needed.
Use high magnification and high NA optics for morphological identification of boutons.
Use live-staining of active boutons or cell-attached recordings for functional identification prior to establishing whole-cell mode.
Prepare a high-K external solution by replacing 40 mM NaCl with KCl stoichiometrically.
Add FM®1-43 to 1 mL of the high-K external solution in a petri dish to achieve a final concentration of 4 μM.
Place the petri dish containing the FM®1-43 and high-K external solution in a dark box.
Insert a fresh coverslip into the petri dish with the solution and incubate for 30–60 seconds in the dark box.
Transfer the coverslip to another petri dish filled with regular external solution for washing.
Subsequently, transfer the coverslip into the recording chamber for imaging.
Identify a bouton for recording.
Immerse the pipette into the bath with moderate positive pressure (20–40 mbar).
Reduce pressure after crossing the bath surface to the minimum level required for solution efflux.
Position the pipette tip in a focal plane just above the targeted bouton.
Set holding potential to nominal 0 mV (minus liquid junction potential).
Monitor pipette resistance using a test pulse.
Set pipette current to zero.
Set the pipette pressure to 5–15 mbar.
Approach the bouton in the direction of the longitudinal pipette axis at minimum micromanipulator speed until you appear to touch the bouton.
Release positive pipette pressure slowly and do not apply suction.
Gently retract the pipette along its longitudinal axis by ∼1 μm to decrease mechanical stress on the bouton membrane.
Determine pipette capacitance using a test pulse.
Compensate for pipette capacitance using the built-in pipette capacitance compensation in cell-attached voltage-clamp mode.
Apply mild suction pulses to break the membrane at the pipette tip.
Monitor membrane intactness using a test pulse to 0 mV (duration 5 ms).
Use test pulse responses to identify sodium and potassium currents indicating membrane rupture.
Optional: Use voltage "zap" protocol with depolarizations from resting potential for 3 ms, starting at 250 mV and increasing in 50 mV increments until whole-cell mode is established.
Upon successful establishment of whole-cell mode, switch amplifier configuration accordingly.
Compensate for pipette capacitance including the capacitance of the pipette holder and the headstage of the amplifier.
Minimize total pipette capacitance.
Record somatic action potentials without compensation of pipette capacitance.
Determine the correct capacitance value in voltage-clamp mode and record somatic action potentials with this compensation.
Record somatic action potentials with small undercompensation of pipette capacitance (-0.25 pF, -0.5 pF).
Record somatic action potentials with overcompensation of pipette capacitance (+0.25 pF, +0.5 pF).
Reduce pipette holder capacitance by shortening connective and electrode wires.
Apply hydrophobic silicone grease on the electrode wire to minimize adhesion of internal solution.
Reduce pipette glass capacitance by using low-capacitance glass types such as quartz glass.
Use minimal pipette immersion with the lowest possible bath solution levels on an inverted microscope.
Prevent adhesion of extra- and intracellular solutions along the glass and silver wire by utilizing the hydrophobicity of quartz glass.
Further prevent adhesion of bath solution along the pipette taper using a steep pipette immersion angle.
Consider lifting the objective from the bath solution after establishing the recording if recordings are performed on an upright microscope.
Apply hydrophobic silicone grease on the pipette taper and tip region under binocular guidance.
Test the effect of different pipette types on bouton recordings prior to data interpretation.
Recommend testing application of silicone grease or extensive coating to borosilicate glass pipettes for capacitance minimization.
